title: Event-Driven Strategy E2E Framework Foundation
goal_statement: Start the local/static/fixture Event-Driven Strategy E2E framework foundation after CR152 ML strategy first-wave closure.
scope_summary: CR153 covers CP0/CP1/CP2 first, then event-driven strategy foundation contracts after approval.

First wave covers EventResearchSpec, three-time semantics, EventStudyMethodSpec, EventRevisionPITGate, event CV slot, universe PIT audit slot, EventStudyTestReport slot, overlap/clustering slot, endogeneity note slot, EventStrategyAdmissionGate and event-to-signal/order-intent trace contract.

CR153 remains local/static/fixture-only and does not authorize real lake, NAS, provider, QMT, runtime, simulation/live/trading, broker, credential, external framework, Git remote, catalog/event/model registry or live event listener operations.

remaining_risks: Fixture/static validation must not be represented as real event feed, runtime readiness, production readiness or trading readiness.
Event-to-order trace contract must remain signal/target/order-intent only until a separate runtime/broker gate is approved.
Method slots for Patell/BMP/bootstrap, clustering and endogeneity must remain slot-only in first wave unless CP2 explicitly expands scope.
EV-GAP-8/9 blocker visibility must be preserved through CV and universe PIT slots even though full governance is deferred to CR154.
split_rationale: CR153 follows CR152 because event-driven methods need a dedicated foundation while reusing shared admission status semantics without mixing event-specific statistics into ML or multifactor gates.
why_not_merge_with_parent: The roadmap is a planning artifact; CR153 needs a formal CP2 scope baseline before design and implementation.
why_not_story_or_task: The change affects event-driven strategy framework scope, admission semantics, testing, evidence and release gates, so it requires formal CR and checkpoint flow.
user_goal_impact: Improves event-driven strategy framework reliability before live event feed, runtime, paper/live or data-lake production work is considered.
